Hi Alyssa / Ben —

Quick kickoff note as we start the renewal conversation for your Oct 1 term:

Goals for this thread:
- Align on capacity uplift options (burst vs. committed GPU pools) and pricing windows
- Schedule a QBR/demo where we walk the new batch-caching and prefix-cache features
- Confirm procurement timeline and any contract/legal constraints so we can plan a rollout

Proposed timeline:
1) This week: share detailed usage + a recommended commit tier for 6/12 months (we did a first pass attached)
2) Next week: 30–45 minute QBR + demo (recommended attendees: engineering lead, procurement, and product owner)
3) Following week: finalize SOW and procurement timeline

Suggested QBR slots: Wed 7/21 10:00–10:45 PDT, Thu 7/22 14:00–14:45 PDT, Fri 7/23 09:00–09:45 PDT. Please tell us which works or send a calendar poll.

A few notes on capacity options we think suit Storix given your traffic pattern:
- Tier A (committed 4x A10G-equivalent): predictable latency, 10% discount vs on-demand
- Tier B (burst + committed baseline): saves ~18% for spiky ingestion weeks, slightly higher tail latency for extreme bursts
- Cache-first: we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for the top 10% of request prefixes — this typically cuts token compute cost by 22% without any model changes

Attachments: Storix_Q2_usage_and_latencY_summary.pdf (summary + heatmaps)

Ask: can you confirm procurement lead and target contract week? If you want, we can also include a short price-option matrix for legal to review.

Thanks —

Alyssa — thanks for the procurement dates, that's helpful. I did a quick pass on commit math and attached two options (6mo/12mo) and a short notes tab for SLO tradeoffs. Highlights: 
- 6mo commit (Tier A): ~12% blended cost reduction, predictable baseline and lower tail latency
- 12mo commit (Tier A+): ~18% blended reduction + better burst crediting for occasional peaks
- Burst+commit hybrid recommended if you expect >3x week-to-week variance; it preserves latency while giving cost savings on baseline load

I'll pull a tightened price matrix (legal-ready) by COB Tue and include explicit SLO language we can slot into an amendment. Also, we can front-load a small canary-capacity migration during the first 30 days to validate caches.
